user.title: Media Time Guard – Person
user.description: Create a media-time budget for one person (usually a child). Enter a name and pick the media players this person uses.

data_description.name: Shown as device name and used by the actions (e.g. `Luke`). Must be unique.
data_description.players: Time counts while at least one of these players is `playing`. Each player can belong to only one person.

budgets.title: Daily budgets
budgets.description: Minutes of media time per weekday. 0 means blocked on that day.

warning.title: Warning
warning.description: Optional one-time warning before the budget runs out. The TTS fields apply when method is TTS; the media fields apply when method is Media.

data_description.warning_threshold: The warning is played once when the remaining time drops to this value.
data_description.tts_message: Leave empty to use the default text in your Home Assistant language. `{minutes}` is replaced by the remaining minutes.

reset.title: Reset
reset.description: Time of day at which the daily count is reset.

data_description.reset_time: Counters, lock, suspension and warning are reset daily at this time.

error.player_in_use: At least one selected media player is already assigned to another person.
error.no_players: Select at least one media player.
error.tts_entity_required: Choose a TTS engine when the warning method is TTS.
error.media_id_required: Enter a media content ID when the warning method is Media.

abort.already_configured: A person with this name is already configured.

init.description: Edit the name and the assigned media players. Renaming keeps the existing entity IDs.

missing_entities.title: Media Time Guard: assigned entities missing for {name}
missing_entities.description:
These entities are assigned to **{name}** but no longer exist: {entities}

If you renamed or replaced a media player or TTS engine, open **Settings → Devices & services → Media Time Guard → {name} → Configure** and select the current entities. Missing media players are neither counted nor stopped.
